newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Donors plan Ivorian agriculture talks late April.
newsitem.headline: Donors plan Ivorian agriculture talks late April.

text.p: Ivory Coast's commodity auction rules will be reviewed by donors and officials during agricultural sector reform talks set to start on April 28, a World Bank official said on Tuesday.
"The auction system will be one of the most important items," said the official. "We will be in Consultative Committee discussions from April 28 to May 10."

Ivory Coast introduced a donor-sponsored cocoa and coffee auction system in May 1996 to improve export contract allocation efficiency and transparency as part of a wider sector liberalisation process.
Exporters have since complained that rules encourage overbidding and lead to price structures out of line with world market rates.

Ivory Coast set up an inter-ministerial Consultative Committee in late 1996 as a forum for government, industry and donor reviews on progress with World Bank Agricultural Sector Adjustment Credit reforms.
Delegates to Committee talks in February aired complaints about auction rules and practices but no solutions were agreed.
"Further talks with industry will be held, maybe in the second half of May," said the Bank official.
World Bank officials recently held contact talks with exporters' representatives ahead of the late April meeting.
